parts.problem_md:
A square has perimeter 12$x$.

Find an expression, in terms of $x$, for the area of the square. Give your answer in its simplest form.
parts.solution_md:
> *Divide the perimeter, *$12x$*, by 4 to find the length of one side (all sides of a square are equal). *

$12x\div4=3x$

**[1]**

> *Square the length of the square to find the area (area of square = length*<sup>*2*</sup>*). *

$( 3 x )^{2} = 9 x^{2}$

**[1]**

$9x^{2}$** [1]**

........................................... cm
parts.solution_md:
> *Find the perimeter of the rectangle and multiply it by 5 (the number of congruent rectangles in the shape). *

$\begin{gathered} 3 + 8 + 3 + 8 & = 22 \\ \\ 22 \times 5 & = 110 \end{gathered}$

> * *

> *Each of the 4 dotted lengths has been counted twice, but they are not parts of the perimeter of the joined-up shape. So subtract 8 lots of 3cm from 110. *

$110 - ( 8 \times 3 ) = 86$

* ***[1]**

**86 cm** **[1]**

parts.problem_md:
![qp4a-0580-32-paper-3-march-2020-cie-igcse-maths](assets/010-qp4a-0580-32-paper-3-march-2020-cie-igcse-maths.png)

The diagram shows the front of Pranav’s house.

i) Work out the total area of the front of his house.

............................................ m<sup>2</sup> [3]

ii) The door is 0.9 m wide and 2.1 m high. Each of the four windows are 1.5 m wide and 1.2 m high.

Work out the total area of the door and the four windows.

............................................ m<sup>2</sup> [3]

iii) Pranav paints the front of his house but not the door and not the four windows.

Work out the area he paints.

............................................ m<sup>2</sup> [1]
parts.solution_md:
i) *Method 1*

> *Split the diagram into a rectangle and a triangle by drawing in a horizontal line at the top of the walls *

> *The formula for the area of a rectangle is: *$A=b\timesh$

> *Substitute *$b=9$* and *$h=5$* into the area formula to determine the area of the rectangle*

$A=9\times5=45$

**[1]**

> *The formula for the area of a triangle is: *$A=0.5\timesb\timesh$

> *Substitute *$b=9$* and *$h=2.4$* into the area formulae to determine the area of the triangle*

$A=0.5\times9\times2.4=10.8$

> *Add the two areas together to get the total area*

> * *$45+10.8$

**[1]**

* *

**55.8 m**<sup>**2**</sup><sup>** **</sup>**[1]**

> * *

> *Method 2*

> *Split the diagram into two equal trapezia *

> *The area of a trapezium is calculated using the formula: *$A = 1 \frac{1}{2} ( a + b ) \times h$* where *$a$* and *$b$* are the two parallel sides and *$h$* is the perpendicular height*

> *Substitute the known values into the formula and evaluate*

$A = 1 \frac{1}{2} \times ( 7.4 + 5 ) \times 4.5 = 27.9$

**[1]**

> *Double this area as both trapezia are equivalent*

$2\times27.9$

**[1]**

**55.8 m**<sup>**2**</sup>** [1]**

** **

ii) *The area of the door (a rectangle) is*

$b\timesh$

$=2.1\times0.9$

$=1.89$

> *The area of the 4 windows (4 rectangles) is*

$( b \times h ) \times 4$

$= ( 1.5 \times 1.2 ) \times 4$

$=7.2$

**[1]**

> $2.1\times0.9$* or *$1.5\times1.2\times4$* or *$1.5\times1.2$* is accepted*

> *The total area of the door and the 4 windows is*

$1.89+7.2=9.09$

**[1]**

**9.09 m**<sup>**2**</sup>** [1]**

** **

iii) *Subtract the area of the door and the windows from the total area of the front of the house*

$55.8-9.09$

** ****46.71 m**<sup>**2**</sup>** ****[1]**

**46.7 is also accepted**

A equals 0.5 cross times b cross times h
A equals 0.5 cross times 9 cross times 2.4 equals 10.8

parts.problem_md:
The length, $l$, of a rectangle is 3 cm longer than the width, $w$.

The perimeter of the rectangle is 26 cm.

Calculate the length, $l$, and the width, $w$.

$l=....................................\mathrm{cm}\,w=...................................\mathrm{cm}$
parts.solution_md:
> *The length, *$l$*, is 3 more than the width, *$w$*.*

> *Write this using algebra. *

$l=w+3$

> * *

![oct-nov-2020-0580-32-q3](assets/014-oct-nov-2020-0580-32-q3.gif)

> * *

> *Add the sides together to find the perimeter and set equal to 26.*

> * *

$w + ( w + 3 ) + w + ( w + 3 ) = 26$

* ***[1]**

> *Collect like terms.*

> * *

$4w+6=26$

> * *

> *Subtract 6 from both sides.*

> * *

$4w=26-6\,4w=20$

* ***[1]**

> *Divide both sides by 4 to solve for *$w$*.*

> * *

$w=20\div4\,w=5$

> * *

* Substitute *$w=5$* into  *$l=w+3$ *to find *$l$*.*

> * *

$l=5+3\,l=8$

> * *

$l=8\mathrm{cm},w=5\mathrm{cm}$* ***[1]**
